title: One-Pan Haloumi and Bean Bake
subtitle: with Crispy Ciabatta
description: Here's a clever spin on baked beans and toast soldiers. Top a tasty bean stew with slices of ciabatta and haloumi, then pop it under the grill for cheesy, crunchy, saucy bliss!

steps.text: Prep ingredients: Cut the tomatoes into 2cm chunks. Thinly slice the spring onion, keeping the white and green parts separate. Crush or finely chop 1 garlic clove. Drain and rinse the beans.

Cook aromatics: Heat 2 tbs olive oil in a medium deep ovenproof frypan over medium heat (see Make it yours). Cook the white part of the spring onion, garlic and country seasoning, stirring, for 1 min or until fragrant. Add 2 tbs tomato paste and cook, stirring, for 30 secs.

Simmer beans: Stir the tomato, beans and 60ml (¼ cup) water into the spring onion mixture. Bring to the boil, then reduce the heat to low and cook, stirring occasionally, for 6-8 mins until the tomato has collapsed and the sauce is slightly reduced. Taste, then season with salt and pepper. Remove the pan from the heat.

Prep topping: Meanwhile, preheat the grill to high. Thinly slice the garlic ciabatta lengthwise. Thinly slice the haloumi widthwise. Arrange the ciabatta and haloumi slices alternately on top of the beans.

Grill and serve up: Put the pan on the middle oven shelf and grill for 6-8 mins until the bread is golden brown and the haloumi is softened. Drizzle with 1 tsp honey and grill for a further 2 mins. Scatter over the remaining spring onion. Divide among plates and enjoy!

Make it yours: If you don't have an ovenproof frypan, you can wrap the handle with a double layer of foil or transfer the bean mixture to an ovenproof dish before topping with the ciabatta and haloumi, then grilling.
